summary: Summit of Pilot Rock on the Christian-Todd county line: a wooden tower was planned in 1952, a USDA tower reportedly built in the 1960s, and ruins were recorded in 2000. A 2013 blog update reports, second-hand, that access was closed.

facts.design: Wooden watchtower, 20 ft (6.1 m), planned in 1952
facts.status_note: The tower is gone; ruins were described on the summit in 2000 and foundation remnants in 2012.

access.note: A 2012 blog says the summit is apparently open to the public and the USDA still owns it, and notes a rumor of private ownership it does not accept. The blog's 2013 update, second-hand, reports a fence blocking access and says the site is supposedly closed. Not confirmed.

visit.trail_note: A short walk to the top, with a parking area for visitors (2012 blog).

events.note: Planned 20-foot wooden watchtower reported; whether it was built is not confirmed
Trip report describes the ruins of the old fire tower on the summit
Blog update, second-hand: a Highway Department fence is reported to block access; site reportedly closed to the public (unconfirmed)

corrections.why: 61.0 m is the 200-ft height of the rock itself, per the 1952 article. The same article gives the planned tower as 20 ft (about 6.1 m). No source gives a built tower height, so the proposed value is the planned height and a reviewer may prefer to clear the field.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1952 page is headed Christian/Todd Counties and the 2012 blog says the rock sits on the county line, so the record's Todd County is kept as one of the two counties.

sources.title: Todd County High Point Trip Report: Pilot Rock

notes_for_editor: The record's height_m of 61.0 is the rock's 200-ft height (see corrections). The 1952 article planned a 20-ft wooden tower; the 2012 blog says the USDA built a fire tower in the 1960s. The sources do not say whether these are the same tower, and no source gives a built height or a build year. The blog is the only source for the USDA ownership, the 1960s tower and the public-access claim. Its 2013 update (a second-hand report of a fence and closure) contradicts the public-access claim, so the access level is now 'disputed' and the story says so; confirm access with the owner before treating the site as public or open. A Reddit post says the tower came down many years ago; it is not cited. The record's coordinates were not checked against a source. The 1952 article also gives the summit elevation as about 900 ft, against 966 ft in the blog; the story uses the blog figure.
